I have implemented [jump_analyzer.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_w6ozrk6/jump_analyzer.py) (mounted at `/app/jump_analyzer.py`) and generated `/app/output.toml` from [example_video.mp4](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_w6ozrk6/example_video.mp4).

### How It Works
- **Background Stabilization & Subtraction ([`analyze_video`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_w6ozrk6/jump_analyzer.py#L8-L143))**: Uses the first frame (`frames[0]`) as the empty-track reference, compensates for sub-pixel camera shake via `cv2.phaseCorrelate` and a `5x5` morphological erosion/dilation envelope, and isolates the athlete's foreground components within the track region.
- **Takeoff & Landing Detection**: Tracks the horizontal median (`x_med`) and lowest vertical foot coordinate (`y_max`) of the athlete across active frames, finds the jump apex over the hurdle (`t_peak`), and identifies:
  - `jump_takeoff_frame_number`: The last ground-contact frame on the takeoff stance plateau immediately preceding the jump (`53` on `example_video.mp4`).
  - `jump_land_frame_number`: The first ground-contact frame on the landing stance plateau immediately following the jump (`62` on `example_video.mp4`).
- **Output Generation ([`main`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_w6ozrk6/jump_analyzer.py#L146-L190))**: Writes the results using `toml` to [output.toml](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_w6ozrk6/output.toml) (`/app/output.toml`).
